Imagine:

• 👨‍🍳 Chef = Call Stack → does the actual work

• 🧾 Order Queue = Callback Queue → waiting tasks

• 🧍‍♂️ Waiter = Event Loop → manages who goes next

🔹 Step 1: JavaScript is Single-Threaded
👉 Only ONE chef in the kitchen
👉 Can do ONE task at a time
So:
console.log("A");
console.log("B");Output:
A
BSimple. One by one.

🔹 Step 2: Problem — What about slow tasks?
setTimeout(() => {
console.log("B");
}, 2000);
console.log("A");If JS waited 2 seconds, everything would freeze 😬
But it doesn’t.

🔹 Step 3: Magic — Web APIs + Queue
Here’s what actually happens:

• "A" goes to Call Stack → executed

• setTimeout is handed to Browser (Web API) ⏳

• Timer runs in background

• "A" finishes → Call Stack becomes empty

• After 2 sec → "B" goes to Callback Queue

🔹 Step 4: Role of Event Loop (THE HERO)
👉 Event Loop keeps checking:
“Is Call Stack empty?
If yes → take next task from Queue”
So:

• Stack empty → Event Loop pushes "B" → executes
Output:
A
B
🔥 One Line Definition (for interviews)
Event Loop is a mechanism that continuously checks the call stack and callback queue, and moves tasks to the stack when it is empty.

⚡ Microtasks vs Macrotasks (VERY IMPORTANT)
Two types of queues:
🟢 Microtasks (HIGH PRIORITY)

• Promise.then

• queueMicrotask
🔵 Macrotasks (LOW PRIORITY)

• setTimeout

• setInterval

• setImmediate
Example:
console.log("A");
setTimeout(() => console.log("B"), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("C"));
console.log("D");Output:
A
D
C
BWhy?

• A → runs

• D → runs

• Microtask © → runs FIRST

• Macrotask (B) → runs LAST

🧠 Memory Trick (Never Forget This)
👉 “Sync → Microtask → Macrotask”
Say it 5 times. That’s the event loop.

💬 How to Explain in Interview
You can say:
“JavaScript is single-threaded, so it uses the event loop to handle async tasks.
Synchronous code runs first in the call stack.
Async tasks like setTimeout go to Web APIs and then to the callback queue.
The event loop moves them back to the stack when it’s empty.
Also, microtasks like Promises run before macrotasks like setTimeout.”
